messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: P1 — Suncrest Health (VPC) auth failures — widespread 401s on private endpoints. Notified on-call.
suncrest_admin: We started seeing 401s ~08:10 UTC. Apps report 'invalid_client' when exchanging code. No changes from our side afaik.
alex: I'm on it. Looking at Redwood side first — checking auth proxy logs for Suncrest VPC pool.
maria: I can confirm the auth-proxy fleet in us-west-2 is rejecting connections from the customer identity proxy. Logs show TLS handshake errors followed by token introspection failing. Sample log:
```
2026-03-15T08:12:04Z auth-proxy[proxy-3] ERROR tls: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-15T08:12:04Z auth-proxy[proxy-3] WARN introspect: jwks fetch failed: 401
```
devops_oncall: Paging infra on-call to check mTLS client cert rotation. Sean, do you have the customer cert rotation notes?
sean: I have their rotation schedule — they rotated client certs yesterday but our mTLS trust bundle shows the old intermediate still present. Hypothesis: their new cert chain omits the intermediate CA and our envoy rejects it as incomplete (chain truncated).
elaine: That would match: handshake fails then introspection falls through. If client cert verification fails early, request never reaches token introspection step.
suncrest_admin: We did rotate certs yesterday via our CA service — we were told it was cross-signed. I'll pull the cert bundle and paste.
suncrest_admin: Paste below (redacted):
```
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF...REDACTED...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
alex: Can you check `openssl verify -show_chain -CAfile ca-bundle.pem client.pem` and confirm chain? If intermediate missing, that explains it.
suncrest_admin: Running now — confirms "unable to get local issuer certificate" for chain step.
devops_oncall: Ok actionable plan:
- temporary mitigation: add a JWKS override on our side to point to customer's static JWKS (bypasses their identity proxy for JWKS only) — short-lived and scoped to Suncrest VPC. This will restore token validation for existing tokens.
- long-term: ask Suncrest to re-issue client cert with full chain (include intermediate), or we accept the intermediate into our trust store after verification.
alex: I'll apply JWKS override to the customer route. Doing it now — adding `override_jwks_url` to route config and doing a rolling restart of auth-proxy instances serving Suncrest.
```
# temp route patch (applied via control-plane)
route: /suncrest/*
override_jwks_url: https://suncrest-internal/suncrest-jwks.json
```
maria: Patching control plane and pushing config. Restarting 3 auth-proxy nodes (proxy-2, proxy-3, proxy-7) one at a time to avoid downtime.
elaine: Monitor metrics: auth success rate and 401 counts, also token-introspect latencies. I created a dashboard panel and set a low-threshold alert to see if things return.
suncrest_admin: After you applied override, our engineers still see some 401s for first-minute requests, probably cached failures. Most calls now show 200s. Thank you.
tom: I looped in Suncrest account team. We're offering to coordinate CA re-issue with them and can accept their intermediate if they sign an MOU. Also prepping a support RCA timeline.
sean: For the permanent fix, recommend Suncrest either:
- re-issue client certs with full chain
- OR publish full CA chain at a stable URL and we'll ingest into our truststore after validation
Also note: we should add a check in our VPC onboarding to verify full client cert chain presence during cert rotation windows.
alex: Post-mitigation checklist:
1) Keep JWKS override in place for 2 hours while we validate no regressions
2) Work with Suncrest to provide full chain
3) Once Suncrest confirms full chain deployed, remove override and restart proxies to pick up new trust bundle
4) Document incident and add automated check to onboarding
maria: Metrics look good — 401s down to baseline after rolling restart. Marking mitigation as successful for now. I'll keep the override flagged with a 2-hour expiry.
suncrest_admin: We'll re-issue certs with intermediate included and ping infra when done. ETA ~2 hours.
devops_oncall: Handoff to next on-call at 10:00 UTC. Current on-call (alex) will be reachable for escalations for 30m.
alex: Logging the incident, will start a postmortem template. Preliminary cause: customer client cert chain truncated on rotation -> mTLS handshake failures -> auth-proxy rejects -> token introspection never completes -> 401s.
elaine: Add action item: add automated cert-chain verification step in our VPC auth integration test harness.
tom: I sent the customer-facing summary and timeline to Suncrest stakeholders and legal (no data exposure). They acknowledged and thanked us.
suncrest_admin: Confirmed re-issue complete, served new bundle with intermediate included. All good on our side.
maria: Removing JWKS override now and restarting final proxy. Will monitor for 10m.
alex: All checks green. Closing the live incident. Will open a postmortem and link infra logs + customer cert artifact.
incident-bot: Incident status -> Resolved (mitigated). Severity: P1 -> Reduced. Postmortem assigned to alex; due in 72h. :white_check_mark:
